title.raw: 卷九 列傳第三 王茂 曹景宗 柳慶遠 Volume 9: Wang Mao; Cao Jingzong; Liu Qingyuan

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第九 列傳第三

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 9, Biographies 3
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume Nine, Biographies, Third

sentences.zh: 王茂 曹景宗 柳慶遠

translations.literal: Wang Mao; Cao Jingzong; Liu Qingyuan
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao; Cao Jingzong; Liu Qingyuan

sentences.zh: 王茂，字休遠，太原祁人也。

translations.literal: Wang Mao, styled Xiuyuan, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mao, styled Xiuyuan, came from Qi in Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖深，北中郎司馬。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shen was Major of the Northern Central Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shen served as major to the Northern Central Commandant.

sentences.zh: 父天生，宋末爲列將，於石頭克司徒袁粲，以勳至巴西、梓潼二郡太守，上黃縣男。

translations.literal: His father Tiansheng in late Song was a ranked general; at Shitou he defeated Minister over the Masses Yuan Can, and by merit rose to Administrator of the two commanderies Brazil and Zitong, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Shanghuang district.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tiansheng, a ranked general in late Song, took Shitou and defeated Minister over the Masses Yuan Can; for merit he became administrator of Brazil and Zitong and was made Marquis of Shanghuang district.

sentences.zh: 茂年數歲，爲大父深所異，常謂親識曰：「此吾家之千里駒，成門戶者必此兒也。

translations.literal: When Mao was only a few years old, his grandfather Shen regarded him as extraordinary and often told acquaintances: "This boy is our family's thousand-li colt; he who will uphold our house must be this child.
translations.idiomatic: While Mao was still a child, his grandfather Shen singled him out and often told friends: "This boy is our thousand-li colt—the one who will uphold our house.

sentences.zh: 」及長，好讀兵書，駁略究其大旨。

translations.literal: " When he grew up, he loved reading books of war and broadly grasped their main purport.
translations.idiomatic: " When he came of age he loved military texts and broadly mastered their essentials.

sentences.zh: 性沈隱，不妄交遊，身長八尺，潔白美容觀。

translations.literal: By nature reserved and self-contained, he did not casually associate; he stood eight chi tall, fair-skinned and handsome in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Reserved by nature, he made no casual friendships; eight chi tall, fair and striking in looks.

sentences.zh: 齊武帝布衣時，見之歎曰：「王茂年少，堂堂如此，必爲公輔之器。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Qi was still in plain dress, seeing him he sighed and said: "Wang Mao is young, yet so imposing; he will surely be minister and counselor material."
translations.idiomatic: Before Emperor Wu of Qi took the throne, he saw Mao and sighed: "So young, yet so imposing—he will surely reach the highest offices."

sentences.zh: 宋昇明末，起家奉朝請，歷後軍行參軍，司空騎兵，太尉中兵參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Song's Shengming era he first entered office as Attendant at Court, and passed through Rear Army Aide, Cavalry of the Minister of Works, and Central Commandant's Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Song's Shengming era he began as Attendant at Court, then served as Rear Army aide, Minister of Works cavalry officer, and Central Commandant's army aide.

sentences.zh: 魏將李烏奴寇漢中，茂受詔西討。

translations.literal: When Wei general Li Wunu raided Hanzhong, Mao received orders for a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei general Li Wunu raided Hanzhong, Mao was ordered west to attack him.

sentences.zh: 魏軍退，還爲鎮南司馬，帶臨湘令。

translations.literal: The Wei army withdrew; he returned as Pacify the South Major, concurrently holding the magistracy of Linxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei withdrew he became Pacify the South major, also serving as magistrate of Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 入爲越騎校尉。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Colonel of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He then entered court as Colonel of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 魏寇兗州，茂時以寧朔將軍長史鎮援北境，入爲前軍將軍江夏王司馬。

translations.literal: When Wei raided Yanzhou, Mao at the time was chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the North, garrisoning the northern border in relief; he entered court as Front Army General's major to the Prince of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei struck Yanzhou, Mao was chief clerk to the General Who Pacifies the North on the northern frontier; he then entered court as major to the Front Army General and Prince of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 又遷寧朔將軍、江夏內史。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to General Who Pacifies the North and Interior Administrator of Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made General Who Pacifies the North and interior administrator of Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 建武初，魏圍司州，茂以郢州之師救焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, Wei besieged Sizhou; Mao led the Yingzhou army to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianwu the Wei besieged Sizhou, and Mao led Yingzhou troops to its relief.

sentences.zh: 高祖率衆先登賢首山，魏將王肅、劉昶來戰，茂從高祖拒之，大破肅等。

translations.literal: Gaozu led the host first to mount Xianshou; Wei generals Wang Su and Liu Chang came to give battle, and Mao followed Gaozu to resist them, greatly defeating Su and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu led the army up Xianshou Mountain first; when Wei generals Wang Su and Liu Chang attacked, Mao followed Gaozu and routed them.

sentences.zh: 魏軍退，茂還郢，仍遷輔國長史、襄陽太守。

translations.literal: The Wei army withdrew; Mao returned to Ying and was then transferred to Support-the-State chief clerk and Administrator of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei withdrew; Mao returned to Ying and was made Support-the-State chief clerk and administrator of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖義師起，茂私於張弘策，勸高祖迎和帝，高祖以爲不然，語在《高祖紀》。

translations.literal: When Gaozu's righteous army rose, Mao privately told Zhang Hongce to urge Gaozu to welcome Emperor He; Gaozu thought otherwise—the account is in the Annals of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu raised the righteous army, Mao privately urged Zhang Hongce to have Gaozu welcome Emperor He; Gaozu disagreed, as told in the Annals of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖發雍部，每遣茂爲前驅。

translations.literal: When Gaozu launched from the Yong region, each time he sent Mao as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Gaozu marched out of Yong, he sent Mao ahead as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 師次郢城，茂進平加湖，破光子衿、吳子陽等，斬馘萬計，還獻捷于漢川。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Ying city, Mao advanced and pacified Jiahu, defeated Guangziqin, Wu Ziyang, and others, and decapitations numbered in the tens of thousands; he returned and presented the victory at Hanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Ying city Mao advanced to pacify Jiahu, defeated Guangziqin and Wu Ziyang, took tens of thousands of heads, and returned to report victory at Hanchuan.

sentences.zh: 郢、魯旣平，從高祖東下，復爲軍鋒。

translations.literal: After Ying and Lu were pacified, he followed Gaozu east and again served as the army's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ying and Lu were pacified, he followed Gaozu east and again led the van.

sentences.zh: 師次秣陵，東昏遣大將王珍國，盛兵朱雀門，衆號二十萬，度航請戰。

translations.literal: When the army reached Moling, Dong Hun sent Grand General Wang Zhenguo, who massed troops at Zhuque Gate; the host was said to number two hundred thousand, and they crossed the floating bridge to request battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Moling, Dong Hun sent Grand General Wang Zhenguo with a host said to number two hundred thousand at Zhuque Gate; they crossed the floating bridge and offered battle.

sentences.zh: 茂與曹景宗等會擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Mao joined Cao Jingzong and others in the attack and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Mao joined Cao Jingzong and others in a combined strike and routed them.

sentences.zh: 縱兵追奔，積屍與航欄等，其赴淮死者，不可勝算。

translations.literal: He released troops in pursuit; corpses piled level with the bridge railings, and those who drowned in the Huai were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He drove the pursuit until corpses stood level with the bridge rails; the dead in the Huai could not be counted.

sentences.zh: 長驅至宣陽門。

translations.literal: They drove in long columns to Xuanyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The army swept on to Xuanyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 建康城平，以茂爲護軍將軍，俄遷侍中、領軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Jiankang was pacified, Mao was made Guard Army General; soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Army Inspector General.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiankang fell, Mao was made Guard Army General, then soon Palace Attendant and Army Inspector General.

sentences.zh: 羣盜之燒神虎門也，茂率所領到東掖門應赴，爲盜所射，茂躍馬而進，羣盜反走。

translations.literal: When bandits burned Divine Tiger Gate, Mao led his command to East Yiji Gate to answer the alarm; shot by bandits, he leapt his horse forward and the bandits turned and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits burned Divine Tiger Gate, Mao rushed his men to East Yiji Gate; though shot at, he spurred forward and the bandits fled.

sentences.zh: 茂以不能式遏姦盜，自表解職，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Because he could not restrain the wicked bandits, Mao memorialized to resign; a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to stop the outlaws, Mao asked to resign; a gracious edict refused.

sentences.zh: 加鎮軍將軍，封望蔡縣公，邑二千三百戶。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title Pacify the Army General and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai county with a fief of two thousand three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made Pacify the Army General and enfeoffed as Duke of Wangcai with two thousand three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 是歲，江州刺史陳伯之舉兵叛，茂出爲使持節、散騎常侍、都督江州諸軍事、征南將軍、江州刺史，給鼓吹一部，南討伯之。

translations.literal: That year Jiangzhou Inspector Chen Bozhi raised troops in rebellion; Mao went out as Bearer of Staff, Scattered Cavalry Attendant, Area Commander of Jiangzhou military affairs, Pacify the South General, and Jiangzhou Inspector, granted one suite of drums and pipes, and marched south to attack Bozhi.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chen Bozhi rebelled as Jiangzhou inspector; Mao went out with staff insignia as Scattered Cavalry Attendant, area commander, Pacify the South General, and Jiangzhou inspector, with drums and pipes, to attack him.

sentences.zh: 伯之奔于魏。

translations.literal: Bozhi fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhi fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 時九江新罹軍寇，民思反業，茂務農省役，百姓安之。

translations.literal: At the time Jiujiang had newly suffered military disaster and the people longed to return to their livelihoods; Mao devoted himself to farming and reducing corvee, and the common people were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang had just been ravaged by war and the people wanted to farm again; Mao pushed farming and cut levies, and the region grew calm.

sentences.zh: 四年，魏侵漢中，茂受詔西討，魏乃班師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Wei invaded Hanzhong; Mao received orders for a western campaign, and Wei then withdrew its army.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Wei invaded Hanzhong; Mao was ordered west, and the Wei army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷尚書右僕射，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, his Palace Attendant post remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year six he became Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing while keeping his Palace Attendant post.

sentences.zh: 固辭不拜，改授侍中、中衛將軍，領太子詹事。

translations.literal: He firmly declined and would not accept; he was instead appointed Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, and concurrent Crown Prince Steward.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined; the appointment was changed to Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, and Crown Prince Steward.

sentences.zh: 七年，拜車騎將軍，太子詹事如故。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Chariots and Cavalry General, Crown Prince Steward remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he was made Chariots and Cavalry General, still Crown Prince Steward.

sentences.zh: 八年，以本號開府儀同三司、丹陽尹，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, under his original title, he received Open Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies and became Danyang Intendant, Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he kept his title but received open office equal to the Three Excellencies and became Danyang intendant, remaining Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時天下無事，高祖方信仗文雅，茂心頗怏怏，侍宴醉後，每見言色，高祖常宥而不之責也。

translations.literal: At the time the realm was at peace and Gaozu was just then trusting literary elegance; Mao's heart was rather displeased, and after feasts when drunk he often showed it in words and countenance—yet Gaozu always pardoned him without blame.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was at peace and Gaozu favored literary men; Mao was ill at ease, and after banquets, drunk, he often showed it in face and speech—yet Gaozu always forgave him.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進位司空，侍中、尹如故。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was advanced to Minister of Works, Palace Attendant and Intendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he was promoted to Minister of Works, keeping Palace Attendant and the intendant post.

sentences.zh: 茂辭京尹，改領中權將軍。

translations.literal: Mao declined the Capital Intendant post and was instead made concurrent Central Authority General.
translations.idiomatic: Mao declined the capital intendant post and took the concurrent Central Authority Generalship instead.

sentences.zh: 茂性寬厚，居官雖無譽，亦爲吏民所安。

translations.literal: Mao was generous and forbearing by nature; though in office he won no special praise, officials and commoners alike were at ease with him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature generous and easy, he won little fame in office, yet officials and people alike trusted him.

sentences.zh: 居處方正，在一室衣冠儼然，雖僕妾莫見其惰容。

translations.literal: In his dwelling he was upright: cap and robes dignified even in a single room, and even concubines never saw him slack in appearance.
translations.idiomatic: At home he kept himself square; even alone in one room his dress was formal, and servants never saw him look lax.

sentences.zh: 姿表瓖麗，鬚眉如畫。

translations.literal: His bearing was splendid and fine; beard and brows were like painted.
translations.idiomatic: He was splendid in bearing, with beard and brows like painted lines.

sentences.zh: 出入朝會，每爲衆所瞻望。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving court assemblies, each time he was gazed upon by the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he attended court, all eyes followed him.

sentences.zh: 明年，出爲使持節、散騎常侍、驃騎將軍、開府同三司之儀、都督江州諸軍事、江州刺史。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Bearer of Staff, Scattered Cavalry Attendant, Fast Cavalry General, Open Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies, Area Commander of Jiangzhou military affairs, and Jiangzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he went out with staff insignia as Scattered Cavalry Attendant, Fast Cavalry General with open office equal to the Three Excellencies, area commander, and Jiangzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 視事三年，薨于州，時年六十。

translations.literal: He administered affairs three years and died in the province at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he died in the province, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 高祖甚悼惜之，賻錢三十萬，布三百匹。

translations.literal: Gaozu deeply mourned him, granting funeral money of three hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu mourned him deeply and granted three hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「旌德紀勳，哲王令軌；

translations.literal: An edict said: "To honor virtue and record merit is the enlightened king's excellent standard;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "To honor virtue and record merit is the enlightened king's true measure;

sentences.zh: 念終追遠，前典明誥。

translations.literal: to think of the end and pursue the distant is the former canon's clear charge.
translations.idiomatic: to remember the dead and reach back to the ancestors is the clear charge of former canons.

sentences.zh: 故使持節、散騎常侍、驃騎將軍、開府儀同三司、江州刺史茂，識度淹廣，器宇凝正。

translations.literal: The late Bearer of Staff, Scattered Cavalry Attendant, Fast Cavalry General, Open Office Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies, and Jiangzhou Inspector Mao had discernment broad and deep and bearing firm and upright.
translations.idiomatic: The late Bearer of Staff, Scattered Cavalry Attendant, Fast Cavalry General, Open Office Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Jiangzhou Inspector Mao was broad in judgment and firm in bearing.

sentences.zh: 爰初草昧，盡誠宣力，綢繆休戚，契闊屯夷。

translations.literal: From the first in hardship and obscurity he devoted loyalty and proclaimed his effort, binding himself in joy and sorrow and sharing ordeals in difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: From the first days of hardship he gave loyal service, sharing joy and sorrow and every trial.

sentences.zh: 方賴謀猷，永隆朝寄；

translations.literal: We were about to rely on his strategies and forever exalt the court's trust;
translations.idiomatic: We meant to rely on his counsel and long entrust him with the court;

sentences.zh: 奄至薨殞，朕用慟于厥心。

translations.literal: suddenly he died, and We are grieved in Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: yet suddenly he died, and Our heart is stricken.

sentences.zh: 宜增禮數，式昭盛烈。

translations.literal: It is fitting to increase the rites and manifest his splendid merit.
translations.idiomatic: His rites should be raised to show forth his great merit.

sentences.zh: 可贈侍中、太尉，加班劍二十人，鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, with twenty Office Swords and one suite of drums and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be granted posthumously Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant, with twenty Office Swords and one suite of drums and pipes.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠烈。」

translations.literal: Posthumous name Loyal and Ardent."
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name Loyal and Ardent."

sentences.zh: 初，茂以元勳，高祖賜以鐘磬之樂。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Mao was a founding merit-holder, Gaozu had granted him the music of bells and chimes.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as a founding merit-holder, Mao had been granted bells and chimes from Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 茂在江州，夢鐘磬在格，無故自墮，心惡之。

translations.literal: While Mao was in Jiangzhou, he dreamed that the bells and chimes on their rack fell for no reason; his heart was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangzhou he dreamed the bells and chimes on their stand fell for no reason, and he took it ill.

sentences.zh: 及覺，命奏樂。

translations.literal: On waking he ordered the music performed.
translations.idiomatic: When he woke he ordered the music played.

sentences.zh: 旣成列，鐘磬在格，果無故編皆絕，墮地。

translations.literal: When the array was complete, the bells and chimes on the rack indeed, for no reason, had all their cords break and fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: When the musicians were in place, every cord on the bells and chimes broke without cause and they crashed to the floor.

sentences.zh: 茂謂長史江詮曰：「此樂，天子所以惠勞臣也。

translations.literal: Mao said to Chief Clerk Jiang Quan: "This music is what the Son of Heaven uses to grace and comfort his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Mao told Chief Clerk Jiang Quan, "This music is what the Son of Heaven grants to reward his ministers.

sentences.zh: 樂旣極矣，能無憂乎！

translations.literal: When music reaches its utmost—can there be no worry!
translations.idiomatic: When music has reached its limit, can there be no foreboding!

sentences.zh: 」俄而病，少日卒。

translations.literal: " Soon after he fell ill, and within a few days died.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon after he fell ill and died within days.

sentences.zh: 子貞秀嗣，以居喪無禮，爲有司奏，徙越州。

translations.literal: His son Zhenxiu succeeded; for observing mourning without propriety he was memorialized by the authorities and banished to Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhenxiu succeeded him but was banished to Yuezhou after the authorities reported his improper mourning.

sentences.zh: 後有詔留廣州，乃潛結仁威府中兵參軍杜景，欲襲州城，刺史蕭昂討之。

translations.literal: Later an edict retained him at Guangzhou; he then secretly joined with Renwei Mansion Army Aide Du Jing to attack the prefectural city, and Inspector Xiao Ang attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict kept him at Guangzhou; he then secretly allied with Renwei Mansion army aide Du Jing to seize the city, and Inspector Xiao Ang put them down.

sentences.zh: 景，魏降人，與貞秀同戮。

translations.literal: Jing was a Wei surrender; he and Zhenxiu were executed together.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, a Wei defector, was executed together with Zhenxiu.

sentences.zh: 曹景宗，字子震，新野人也。

translations.literal: Cao Jingzong, styled Zizhen, was a native of Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Jingzong, styled Zizhen, came from Xinye.

sentences.zh: 父欣之，爲宋將，位至征虜將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Xinbei was a Song general who reached Pacify the Barbarians General and Xuzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xinbei was a Song general who rose to Pacify the Barbarians General and inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 景宗幼善騎射，好畋獵。

translations.literal: Jingzong in youth was skilled at riding and shooting and loved hunting.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Jingzong excelled at riding and archery and loved the chase.

sentences.zh: 常與少年數十人澤中逐麞鹿，每衆騎赴鹿，鹿馬相亂，景宗於衆中射之，人皆懼中馬足，鹿應弦輒斃，以此爲樂。

translations.literal: He often went with several dozen youths into the marshes to chase deer; when the crowd galloped at the deer, deer and horses became a chaos, yet Jingzong shot among them—everyone feared he would hit a horse's leg, but the deer at the bowstring's release always fell dead; he took this as his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He often rode with dozens of youths through the marshes after deer; when horses and deer tangled in the rush, he shot into the melee—men feared he would hit their mounts, yet every arrow dropped a deer, which he found delightful.

sentences.zh: 未弱冠，欣之於新野遣出州，以匹馬將數人，於中路卒逢蠻賊數百圍之。

translations.literal: Before he had reached the weak-crown age, Xinbei at Xinye sent him out of the province with one horse and a few men; on the road he suddenly met several hundred Man bandits surrounding him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he came of age, Xinbei sent him out of Xinye with one horse and a few followers; on the road several hundred Man bandits suddenly surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 景宗帶百餘箭，乃馳騎四射，每箭殺一蠻，蠻遂散走，因是以膽勇知名。

translations.literal: Jingzong carried more than a hundred arrows; he then galloped and shot in four directions, each arrow killing one barbarian, and the barbarians scattered and fled—thereby he became known for bold courage.
translations.idiomatic: He carried more than a hundred arrows, wheeled his horse, and shot in every direction, killing one tribesman with each shaft until they broke and fled; from then on he was famed for courage.

sentences.zh: 頗愛史書，每讀《穰苴》、《樂毅傳》，輒放卷歎息曰：「丈夫當如是！

translations.literal: He quite loved historical writings; whenever he read the Records of Rang Ju and the Biography of Yue Yi, he would put down the scroll and sigh: "A man should be like this!
translations.idiomatic: He loved history; reading the Records of Rang Ju and the Biography of Yue Yi, he would close the scroll and sigh, "A man should be like this!

sentences.zh: 」辟西曹不就。

translations.literal: " He declined appointment to the Western Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " He declined appointment to the Western Bureau.

sentences.zh: 宋元徽中，隨父出京師，爲奉朝請、員外，遷尚書左民郎。

translations.literal: In Yuanhui of Song he followed his father to the capital, served as Attendant at Court and Outer Member, and was transferred to Left People Officer of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In Song's Yuanhui era he followed his father to the capital as Attendant at Court and outer member, then became Left People Officer in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 尋以父憂去職，還鄉里。

translations.literal: Soon, on his father's death, he left office and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his father died; he left office and went home.

sentences.zh: 服闋，刺史蕭赤斧板爲冠軍中兵參軍，領天水太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Inspector Xiao Chifu commissioned him as Champion Army Aide, concurrently Administrator of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning, Inspector Xiao Chifu made him Champion Army aide and concurrent administrator of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 時建元初，蠻寇羣動，景宗東西討擊，多所擒破。

translations.literal: At the time, early in Jianyuan, Man bandits were active everywhere; Jingzong campaigned east and west, capturing and defeating many.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyuan, when Man raiders rose on every side, Jingzong campaigned east and west and took many captives.

sentences.zh: 齊鄱陽王鏘爲雍州，復以爲征虜中兵參軍，帶馮翊太守，督峴南諸軍事，除屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: When Qi's Prince of Poyang Xiao Zhen held Yongzhou, Jingzong was again made Pacify the Barbarians Army Aide, concurrently Administrator of Fengyi, supervised military affairs south of Xian, and was promoted to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Poyang Xiao Zhen became inspector of Yongzhou, Jingzong was again made Pacify the Barbarians army aide and administrator of Fengyi, supervised troops south of Xian, and was promoted to Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 少與州里張道門厚善。

translations.literal: In youth he was on close terms with his fellow townsman Zhang Daomen.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was close to a townsman, Zhang Daomen.

sentences.zh: 道門，齊車騎將軍敬兒少子也，爲武陵太守。

translations.literal: Daomen was the youngest son of Qi's Chariots and Cavalry General Jinger and served as Administrator of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Daomen was the youngest son of Qi's Chariots and Cavalry General Zhang Jinger and was administrator of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 敬兒誅，道門於郡伏法，親屬故吏莫敢收，景宗自襄陽遣人船到武陵，收其屍骸，迎還殯葬，鄉里以此義之。

translations.literal: When Jinger was executed, Daomen was executed in the commandery; kin and former subordinates none dared collect the corpse—yet Jingzong sent men and boats from Xiangyang to Wuling, collected the remains, and returned them for burial; the hometown therefore honored his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinger was put to death, Daomen was executed in the commandery and none of kin or former staff dared claim the body; Jingzong sent men and boats from Xiangyang to Wuling, recovered the corpse, and buried it at home—the district praised his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，魏主托跋宏寇赭陽，景宗爲偏將，每衝堅陷陣，輒有斬獲，以勳除遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, Wei ruler Tuoba Hong raided Zheyang; Jingzong was a supporting general and each charge broke the enemy line, with beheadings each time; by merit he was made Raids General.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year two Tuoba Hong of Wei raided Zheyang; Jingzong was a flank commander, broke the line each time he charged, and was made Raids General for merit.

sentences.zh: 四年，太尉陳顯達督衆軍北圍馬圈，景宗從之，以甲士二千設伏，破魏援托跋英四萬人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Grand Commandant Chen Xianda commanded the armies north to besiege Maquan; Jingzong followed him and, with two thousand armored men, set an ambush and defeated Wei relief under Tuoba Ying—forty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Grand Commandant Chen Xianda besieged Maquan in the north; Jingzong followed with two thousand armored men in ambush and routed forty thousand Wei troops under Tuoba Ying.

sentences.zh: 及剋馬圈，顯達論功，以景宗爲後，景宗退無怨言。

translations.literal: When Maquan was taken, Xianda assessed merit and ranked Jingzong last; Jingzong withdrew without complaint.
translations.idiomatic: When Maquan fell, Xianda ranked the merit and put Jingzong last; Jingzong withdrew without a word.

sentences.zh: 魏主率衆大至，顯達宵奔，景宗導入山道，故顯達父子獲全。

translations.literal: The Wei ruler led a great army up; Xianda fled by night, and Jingzong guided him into mountain paths—therefore Xianda and his son were wholly saved.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei ruler came in force; Xianda fled by night, and Jingzong led him through the mountains, so Xianda and his son escaped whole.

sentences.zh: 五年，高祖爲雍州刺史，景宗深自結附，數請高祖臨其宅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Gaozu was Yongzhou Inspector; Jingzong attached himself deeply and repeatedly invited Gaozu to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Gaozu was inspector of Yongzhou; Jingzong courted him closely and often asked him to his house.

sentences.zh: 時天下方亂，高祖亦厚加意焉。

translations.literal: At the time the realm was in disorder, and Gaozu also greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in turmoil, and Gaozu in turn treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 永元初，表爲冠軍將軍、竟陵太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongyuan he was memorialized as Champion General and Administrator of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yongyuan he was recommended as Champion General and administrator of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 及義師起，景宗聚衆，遣親人杜思沖勸先迎南康王於襄陽卽帝位，然後出師，爲萬全計。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Jingzong gathered troops and sent his kinsman Du Sichong to urge that they first welcome the Prince of Nankang at Xiangyang to ascend the throne and then march— a plan for complete security.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, Jingzong mustered troops and sent his kinsman Du Sichong to urge welcoming the Prince of Nankang at Xiangyang as emperor before marching— a plan for perfect safety.

sentences.zh: 高祖不從，語在《高祖紀》。

translations.literal: Gaozu did not follow—the account is in the Annals of Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused, as told in the Annals of Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖至竟陵，以景宗與冠軍將軍王茂濟江，圍郢城，自二月至於七月，城乃降。

translations.literal: When Gaozu reached Jingling, he made Jingzong and Champion General Wang Mao cross the river and besiege Ying city; from the second month to the seventh the city then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingling Gaozu sent Jingzong and Champion General Wang Mao across the river to besiege Ying; from the second month to the seventh month the city surrendered.

sentences.zh: 復帥衆前驅至南州，領馬步軍取建康。

translations.literal: He again led troops as vanguard to Nanzhou and commanded horse and foot to take Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He again led the van to Nanzhou and commanded horse and foot against Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 道次江寧，東昏將李居士以重兵屯新亭，是日選精騎一千至江寧行頓，景宗始至，安營未立；

translations.literal: Passing Jiangning, Dong Hun's general Li Jushi held Xinting with heavy troops; that day he selected a thousand elite cavalry to Jiangning marching halt—Jingzong had just arrived and his camp was not yet set;
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangning, Dong Hun's general Li Jushi held Xinting with a heavy force; that day he sent a thousand picked horsemen to Jingzong's halt—Jingzong had just arrived and his camp was not yet pitched;

sentences.zh: 且師行日久，器甲穿弊，居士望而輕之，因鼓噪前薄景宗。

translations.literal: moreover the army had marched long and weapons and armor were worn through; Jushi seeing this despised them and therefore beat drums, clamored, and pressed forward close on Jingzong.
translations.idiomatic: and the column had marched long, its arms in tatters; Jushi saw this, despised them, and charged with drums and shouts straight at Jingzong.

sentences.zh: 景宗被甲馳戰，短兵裁接，居士棄甲奔走，景宗皆獲之，因鼓而前，徑至皁莢橋築壘。

translations.literal: Jingzong donned armor and galloped to battle; in close combat they had barely joined when Jushi abandoned his armor and fled; Jingzong captured them all, then drummed forward and went straight to Zaojia Bridge to build a rampart.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong armored and rode to meet them; in close fight Jushi threw off his armor and ran; Jingzong took them all, drummed forward, and built a rampart at Zaojia Bridge.

sentences.zh: 景宗又與王茂、呂僧珍掎角，破王珍國於大航。

translations.literal: Jingzong again joined Wang Mao and Lu Sengzhen in a pincer attack and defeated Wang Zhenguo at the Great Floating Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong again joined Wang Mao and Lu Sengzhen in a pincer and defeated Wang Zhenguo at the Great Floating Bridge.

sentences.zh: 茂衝其中堅，應時而陷，景宗縱兵乘之。

translations.literal: Mao charged the hard center and it fell at once; Jingzong released troops to exploit the victory.
translations.idiomatic: Mao broke the enemy center and it collapsed at once; Jingzong drove the troops to press the rout.

sentences.zh: 景宗軍士皆桀黠無賴，御道左右，莫非富室，抄掠財物，略奪子女，景宗不能禁。

translations.literal: Jingzong's soldiers were all fierce and unbridled ruffians; along the imperial avenue, right and left, there were none but wealthy houses—they looted goods and seized women and children, and Jingzong could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong's men were violent and lawless; along the imperial way every house was rich, and they plundered goods and seized women and children—Jingzong could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 及高祖入頓新城，嚴申號令，然後稍息。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered and encamped at Xincheng, he strictly enforced orders, and only then did things gradually quiet.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered and encamped at Xincheng, he enforced orders strictly, and only then did the turmoil subside.

sentences.zh: 復與衆軍長圍六門。

translations.literal: He again joined the massed armies in a long siege of the Six Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the armies in a long siege of the Six Gates.

sentences.zh: 城平，拜散騎常侍、右衛將軍，封湘西縣侯，食邑一千六百戶。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Jingzong was appointed Regular Attendant, Right Guard General, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangxi with a fief of one thousand six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he was made Regular Attendant and Right Guard General, enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiangxi with a fief of sixteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 仍遷持節、都督郢司二州諸軍事、左將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Ying and Si provinces, Left General, and Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Bearer of the Staff, commander-in-chief of Ying and Si provinces, Left General, and inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，進號平西將軍，改封竟陵縣侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 1 he was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 景宗在州，鬻貨聚斂。

translations.literal: While Jingzong held the province, he trafficked in goods and amassed wealth.
translations.idiomatic: While holding the province, Jingzong trafficked in goods and amassed wealth.

sentences.zh: 於城南起宅，長堤以東，夏口以北，開街列門，東西數里，而部曲殘橫，民頗厭之。

translations.literal: South of the city he built a mansion; east of the Long Embankment and north of Xiakou he opened streets and set gates for several li east and west, while his retainers were brutal and overbearing—the people greatly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: South of the city he built a mansion; east of the Long Embankment and north of Xiakou he laid out streets and gates for miles east and west, while his retainers ran wild—the people deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 二年十月，魏寇司州，圍刺史蔡道恭。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year, Wei raided Si province and besieged Inspector Cai Daogong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of year 2, Wei raided Si province and besieged the inspector Cai Daogong.

sentences.zh: 時魏攻日苦，城中負板而汲，景宗望門不出，但耀軍遊獵而已。

translations.literal: As Wei's assault grew daily harsher, the cityfolk carried boards on their backs to draw water; Jingzong watched from the gate and would not go out, but only displayed his troops in hunts.
translations.idiomatic: As the Wei assault grew harsher by the day, people in the city drew water under shield; Jingzong watched from the gate and would not emerge, parading his troops in hunts alone.

sentences.zh: 及司州城陷，爲御史中丞任昉所奏。

translations.literal: When Si province's city fell, he was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang.
translations.idiomatic: When Si province fell, Censor-in-Chief Ren Fang impeached him.

sentences.zh: 高祖以功臣寢而不治，徵爲護軍。

translations.literal: Gaozu, because he was a meritorious minister who had grown lax and gone unpunished, summoned him to be Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, treating him as a meritorious minister grown lax and left unpunished, summoned him to be Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 旣至，復拜散騎常侍、右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he was again appointed Regular Attendant and Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he was again made Regular Attendant and Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 五年，魏托跋英寇鐘離，圍徐州刺史昌義之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Tuoba Ying of Wei raided Zhongli and besieged Xuzhou Inspector Chang Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, Tuoba Ying of Wei raided Zhongli and besieged Xuzhou inspector Chang Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔景宗督衆軍援義之，豫州刺史韋叡亦預焉，而受景宗節度。

translations.literal: Gaozu ordered Jingzong to command the massed armies to relieve Yizhi; Yuzhou Inspector Wei Rui also took part, but was placed under Jingzong's command.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu ordered Jingzong to command the armies to relieve Yizhi; Yuzhou inspector Wei Rui joined as well, under Jingzong's command.

sentences.zh: 詔景宗頓道人洲，待衆軍齊集俱進。

translations.literal: He ordered Jingzong to encamp at Daoren Isle and wait until all the armies had gathered to advance together.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jingzong to encamp at Daoren Isle and wait for the armies to gather before advancing together.

sentences.zh: 景宗固啓，求先據邵陽洲尾，高祖不聽。

translations.literal: Jingzong repeatedly memorialized, asking to seize the tail of Shaoyang Isle first; Gaozu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong repeatedly petitioned to seize the end of Shaoyang Isle first; Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 景宗欲專其功，乃違詔而進，值暴風卒起，頗有渰溺，復還守先頓。

translations.literal: Jingzong wished to monopolize the merit, so he disobeyed the edict and advanced; a sudden storm arose and many were drowned, and he returned to hold his former camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to keep the glory for himself, Jingzong disobeyed the edict and advanced; a sudden storm drowned many, and he fell back to his former camp.

sentences.zh: 高祖聞之，曰：「此所以破賊也。

translations.literal: When Gaozu heard of it, he said: "This is how the enemy will be broken.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu heard, he said, "This is how we break the enemy.

sentences.zh: 景宗不進，蓋天意乎！

translations.literal: If Jingzong does not advance, is it not Heaven's will!
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong holding back—surely that is Heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 若孤軍獨往，城不時立，必見狼狽。

translations.literal: If a lone army went alone, the ramparts would not be raised in time and one would surely be reduced to disarray.
translations.idiomatic: Had he marched alone, the fort would not have risen in time and the army would have come to grief.

sentences.zh: 今得待衆軍同進，始大捷矣。

translations.literal: Now that all the armies may advance together, there will truly be a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Now we can wait for every army to advance together, and the great victory will come.

sentences.zh: 」及韋叡至，與景宗進頓邵陽洲，立壘去魏城百餘步。

translations.literal: " When Wei Rui arrived, he and Jingzong advanced and encamped at Shaoyang Isle, building ramparts within a hundred-odd paces of the Wei city.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Rui arrived, he and Jingzong advanced to Shaoyang Isle and built ramparts a little over a hundred paces from the Wei city.

sentences.zh: 魏連戰不能却，殺傷者十二三，自是魏軍不敢逼。

translations.literal: Wei fought repeatedly but could not drive them off; those killed and wounded were two or three in ten, and from then on the Wei army did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: Wei attacked again and again but could not drive them back; casualties ran to two or three in ten, and thereafter the Wei army did not dare close in.

sentences.zh: 景宗等器甲精新，軍儀甚盛，魏人望之奪氣。

translations.literal: Jingzong and the others had armor and weapons fresh and fine, and their military array was very grand; the Wei men gazed upon them and lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong and the rest had bright new arms and armor and a splendid array; the Wei troops looked on and lost heart.

sentences.zh: 魏大將楊大眼對橋北岸立城，以通糧運，每牧人過岸伐芻槁，皆爲大眼所略。

translations.literal: Wei's great general Yang Dayan built a city on the north bank opposite the bridge to keep grain transport open; whenever herders crossed the bank to cut fodder, Dayan seized them all.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's great general Yang Dayan built a city on the north bank opposite the bridge to keep supplies moving; whenever herders crossed to cut fodder, Dayan seized them.

sentences.zh: 景宗乃募勇敢士千餘人，徑渡大眼城南數里築壘，親自舉築。

translations.literal: Jingzong then recruited more than a thousand brave men, crossed straight over several li south of Dayan's city, and built a rampart, raising the earthworks himself.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong then recruited more than a thousand brave men, crossed several li south of Dayan's city, and built a rampart, piling earth with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 大眼率衆來攻，景宗與戰破之，因得壘成。

translations.literal: Dayan led his host to attack; Jingzong fought and defeated him, and so the rampart was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Dayan led his troops to attack; Jingzong fought and broke him, and the rampart was finished.

sentences.zh: 使別將趙草守之，因謂爲趙草城，是後恣芻牧焉。

translations.literal: He sent the separate commander Zhao Cao to hold it, and therefore called it Fort Zhao Cao; thereafter they grazed fodder at will.
translations.idiomatic: He left the separate commander Zhao Cao to hold it, and the place was called Fort Zhao Cao; thereafter they grazed fodder freely.

sentences.zh: 大眼時遣抄掠，輒反爲趙草所獲。

translations.literal: Whenever Dayan sent parties to raid, they were in turn captured by Zhao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Dayan sent raiders, Zhao Cao captured them instead.

sentences.zh: 先是，高祖詔景宗等逆裝高艦，使與魏橋等，爲火攻計。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gaozu had ordered Jingzong and the others to fit out tall warships in advance, to match the Wei bridges in height, for a fire-attack plan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gaozu had ordered Jingzong and the others to fit out tall warships in advance, level with the Wei bridges, for a fire attack.

sentences.zh: 令景宗與叡各攻一橋，叡攻其南，景宗攻其北。

translations.literal: He ordered Jingzong and Rui each to attack one bridge—Rui the south, Jingzong the north.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jingzong and Rui each to take one bridge—Rui the south, Jingzong the north.

sentences.zh: 六年三月，春水生，淮水暴長六七尺。

translations.literal: In the third month of the sixth year the spring waters rose and the Huai surged six or seven feet.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year 6 the spring flood came and the Huai rose six or seven feet overnight.

sentences.zh: 叡遣所督將馮道根、李文釗、裴邃、韋寂等乘艦登岸，擊魏洲上軍盡殪。

translations.literal: Rui sent the generals under his command—Feng Daogen, Li Wenzhao, Pei Sui, Wei Ji, and others—to board the warships, land, and annihilate the Wei troops on the isle.
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent Feng Daogen, Li Wenzhao, Pei Sui, Wei Ji, and other generals under his command to land from the ships and slaughter the Wei troops on the isle.

sentences.zh: 景宗因使衆軍皆鼓噪亂登諸城，呼聲震天地，大眼於西岸燒營，英自東岸棄城走。

translations.literal: Jingzong then had all the armies drum and shout and scramble up the walls in disorder; the clamor shook heaven and earth; Dayan burned his camp on the west bank, and Ying abandoned his city and fled from the east bank.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong then had every army drum and shout and swarm the walls; the roar shook heaven and earth; Dayan burned his camp on the west bank, and Ying abandoned his city and fled from the east.

sentences.zh: 諸壘相次土崩，悉棄其器甲，爭投水死，淮水爲之不流。

translations.literal: Rampart after rampart collapsed like earthworks; all cast away arms and armor and strove to throw themselves into the water and die—the Huai was choked so that it would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Rampart after rampart crumbled; all cast off arms and armor and threw themselves into the water to die—the Huai was so choked it would not flow.

sentences.zh: 景宗令軍主馬廣躡大眼至濊水上，四十餘里，伏屍相枕。

translations.literal: Jingzong ordered the army commander Ma Guang to pursue Dayan to the Huishui River for more than forty li; corpses lay pillow to pillow.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong ordered the army commander Ma Guang to pursue Dayan to the Huishui for more than forty li; the dead lay heaped along the way.

sentences.zh: 義之出逐英至洛口，英以匹馬入梁城。

translations.literal: Yizhi went out in pursuit of Ying to Luokou; Ying entered Liang city on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi pursued Ying to Luokou; Ying entered Liang city on a single horse.

sentences.zh: 緣淮百餘里，屍骸枕藉，生擒五萬餘人，收其軍糧器械，積如山岳，牛馬驢騾，不可勝計。

translations.literal: For more than a hundred li along the Huai, corpses lay pillow to pillow; more than fifty thousand were taken alive; grain, weapons, and equipment were gathered in heaps like mountains; oxen, horses, donkeys, and mules were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: For more than a hundred li along the Huai the dead lay piled; more than fifty thousand were captured alive; grain and arms heaped like mountains; cattle, horses, donkeys, and mules beyond count.

sentences.zh: 景宗乃搜軍所得生口萬餘人，馬千匹，遣獻捷，高祖詔還本軍，景宗振旅凱入，增封四百，並前爲二千戶，進爵爲公。

translations.literal: Jingzong then searched out more than ten thousand captives and a thousand horses from what the army had taken, sent them to report victory, and Gaozu ordered him back to his original command; Jingzong led his troops home in triumph, his fief was increased by four hundred households to two thousand in all, and he was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong gathered more than ten thousand captives and a thousand horses from the army's takings and sent word of victory; Gaozu ordered him back to his command; Jingzong marched home in triumph, his fief was increased by four hundred households to two thousand in all, and he was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 詔拜侍中、領軍將軍，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: By edict he was appointed Palace Attendant and Commander of the Army, with one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was made Palace Attendant and Commander of the Army, with one set of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 景宗爲人自恃尚勝，每作書，字有不解，不以問人，皆以意造焉。

translations.literal: Jingzong was by nature self-reliant and fond of outdoing others; whenever he wrote letters, if he did not understand a character he would not ask anyone, but invent it as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong was proud and always had to win; when he wrote, any character he did not know he would not ask about but invent as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 雖公卿無所推揖；

translations.literal: Though among dukes and ministers he showed no deference;
translations.idiomatic: He showed no deference even to dukes and ministers;

sentences.zh: 惟韋叡年長，且州里勝流，特相敬重，同宴御筵，亦曲躬謙遜，高祖以此嘉之。

translations.literal: only Wei Rui was older and a leading figure of their native district, and he specially respected him; at banquets on the imperial mat he too bowed with humble courtesy—Gaozu praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: only Wei Rui, who was older and a leading man of their district, he specially honored; at imperial banquets he bowed with humble courtesy as well—Gaozu praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 景宗好內，妓妾至數百，窮極錦繡。

translations.literal: Jingzong was fond of women; his singing girls and concubines numbered in the hundreds, and he exhausted brocades and embroideries.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong loved women; his concubines and singing girls numbered in the hundreds, and he exhausted every brocade and embroidery.

sentences.zh: 性躁動，不能沈默，出行常欲褰車帷幔，左右輒諫以位望隆重，人所具瞻，不宜然。

translations.literal: By nature restless, he could not keep silent; when he went out he always wanted to lift the carriage curtains, and those at his side would remonstrate that his rank and standing were weighty and that all eyes were upon him—he ought not do so.
translations.idiomatic: Restless by nature, he could not keep still; on the road he always wanted to throw back the carriage curtains, and his attendants would warn him that with his rank and dignity all eyes were on him—he should not.

sentences.zh: 景宗謂所親曰：「我昔在鄉里，騎快馬如龍，與年少輩數十騎，拓弓弦作霹靂聲，箭如餓鴟叫。

translations.literal: Jingzong said to those close to him: "In the old days at home I rode a swift horse like a dragon, with several dozen young fellows, drawing the bowstring till it cracked like thunder, arrows shrieking like hungry kites.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong told his intimates: "Back home I rode a swift horse like a dragon, with several dozen young men at my side, drawing the bowstring till it thundered, arrows screaming like hungry kites.

sentences.zh: 平澤中逐麞，數肋射之，渴飲其血，饑食其肉，甜如甘露漿。

translations.literal: In the open marsh we chased deer; I shot them through the ribs several times, drank their blood when thirsty and ate their flesh when hungry—sweet as sweet dew.
translations.idiomatic: On the open marsh we chased deer; I shot them through the ribs again and again, drank their blood when thirsty, ate their flesh when hungry—sweet as nectar.

sentences.zh: 覺耳後風生，鼻頭出火，此樂使人忘死，不知老之將至。

translations.literal: I felt wind rise behind my ears and fire burst from my nostrils—such joy makes one forget death and not know that old age is coming.
translations.idiomatic: Wind rose behind my ears, fire seemed to burst from my nostrils—joy like that makes you forget death and never feel old age draw near.

sentences.zh: 今來揚州作貴人，動轉不得，路行開車幔，小人輒言不可。

translations.literal: Now I have come to Yangzhou to be a great man and cannot stir; on the road I open the carriage curtains and petty men say I must not.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have come to Yangzhou to play the great man and cannot move; on the road I lift the carriage curtain and little men say I must not.

sentences.zh: 閉置車中，如三日新婦。

translations.literal: Shut up in the carriage like a bride of three days.
translations.idiomatic: Shut in the carriage like a bride on her third day.

sentences.zh: 遭此邑邑，使人無氣。

translations.literal: To suffer such vexation takes the breath from a man.
translations.idiomatic: This suffocation steals a man's breath.

sentences.zh: 」爲人嗜酒好樂，臘月於宅中，使作野虖逐除，遍往人家乞酒食。

translations.literal: " He was by nature addicted to wine and fond of music; in the twelfth month at his mansion he had a wilderness howl performed for the year-end expulsion, going from house to house begging wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and music; in the twelfth month at his mansion he staged the wilderness howl for the year-end expulsion, going door to door begging wine and food.

sentences.zh: 本以爲戲，而部下多剽輕，因弄人婦女，奪人財貨。

translations.literal: He had meant it as sport, but many of his subordinates were violent and light-minded, and so molested other men's wives and seized people's goods.
translations.idiomatic: It was meant as sport, but many of his men were violent and took liberties with women and seized property.

sentences.zh: 高祖頗知之，景宗乃止。

translations.literal: Gaozu came to know of it fairly well, and Jingzong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu learned of it, and Jingzong then stopped.

sentences.zh: 高祖數讌見功臣，共道故舊，景宗醉後謬忘，或誤稱下官，高祖故縱之，以爲笑樂。

translations.literal: Gaozu often feasted the meritorious ministers and talked over old times together; after wine Jingzong would forget himself in error and sometimes wrongly call himself "your servant"; Gaozu deliberately indulged him and took it as laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu often feasted his merit-holders and talked of old times; drunk, Jingzong would forget himself and sometimes call himself "your servant"; Gaozu indulged it and laughed.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷侍中、中衛將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was transferred to Palace Attendant, Central Guard General, and inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 赴任卒於道，時年五十二。

translations.literal: On the way to his post he died on the road, aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the road while going to his post, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 詔賻錢二十萬，布三百匹，追贈征北將軍、雍州刺史、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: By edict he was granted two hundred thousand in cash and three hundred bolts of cloth; posthumously he was made General Who Campaigns North, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: By edict he was granted two hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth; posthumously he was made General Who Campaigns North, inspector of Yongzhou, and Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 諡曰壯。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Zhuang, "Strong."

sentences.zh: 子皎嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jiao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiao succeeded.

sentences.zh: 柳慶遠，字文和，河東解人也。

translations.literal: Liu Qingyuan, styled Wenhe, was a man of Jie in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qingyuan, styled Wenhe, came from Jie in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 伯父元景，宋太尉。

translations.literal: His father's elder brother Yuanjing was Song Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: His father's elder brother Yuanjing had been Song Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 慶遠起家郢州主簿，齊初爲尚書都官郎、大司馬中兵參軍、建武將軍、魏興太守。

translations.literal: Qingyuan began his career as Registrar of Yingzhou; at the start of Qi he was Director of the Ministry of Justice in the Masters of Writing, Central Army Aide of the Grand Marshal, General Who Establishes Martial Prowess, and Administrator of Weixing.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan began as registrar of Yingzhou; at the start of Qi he was Director in the Ministry of Justice, central army aide to the Grand Marshal, General Who Establishes Martial Prowess, and administrator of Weixing.

sentences.zh: 郡遭暴水，流漂居民，吏請徙民祀城。

translations.literal: The commandery suffered a sudden flood that swept away the people; the clerks asked to move the people to sacrifice at the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery was struck by sudden floodwaters that swept away the people; the clerks asked to move them to sacrifice at the city wall.

sentences.zh: 慶遠曰：「天降雨水，豈城之所知。

translations.literal: Qingyuan said: "Heaven sends down rain—how would the city know?
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan said, "Heaven sends rain—how would the city know?

sentences.zh: 吾聞江河長不過三日，斯亦何慮。

translations.literal: I have heard that rivers and streams do not rise for more than three days—what is there to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: I have heard rivers do not rise more than three days—what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 」命築土而已。

translations.literal: " He ordered only earthworks built.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered only earth ramparts built.

sentences.zh: 俄而水過，百姓服之。

translations.literal: Before long the waters passed, and the people submitted to his judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the waters receded, and the people admired his judgment.

sentences.zh: 入爲長水校尉，出爲平北錄事參軍、襄陽令。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Colonel of the Long River Guard and went out as Recorder of the Pacify North Staff and Magistrate of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Colonel of the Long River Guard and went out as recorder on the Pacify North staff and magistrate of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖之臨雍州，問京兆人杜惲求州綱，惲舉慶遠。

translations.literal: When Gaozu came to Yongzhou, he asked the man of Jingzhao, Du Yun, for the province's leading men; Yun recommended Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took Yongzhou, he asked Du Yun of Jingzhao for the province's leading men; Yun recommended Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「文和吾已知之，所問未知者耳。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "I already know Wenhe; what I asked about was what I did not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "I already know Wenhe; I was asking about what I did not yet know.

sentences.zh: 」因辟別駕從事史。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he summoned him as Aide-de-Camp Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he summoned him as aide-de-camp attendant.

sentences.zh: 齊方多難，慶遠謂所親曰：「方今天下將亂，英雄必起，庇民定霸，其吾君乎？

translations.literal: Qi was then beset by many troubles; Qingyuan said to those close to him: "The realm under heaven will soon fall into disorder; heroes are sure to rise—he who shelters the people and settles hegemony, is he not our lord?
translations.idiomatic: Qi was then in turmoil; Qingyuan told his intimates, "The realm will soon fall into disorder; heroes are sure to rise—he who shelters the people and settles hegemony, is he not our lord?

sentences.zh: 」因盡誠協贊。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he devoted himself fully in loyal support.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he gave himself wholly to loyal support.

sentences.zh: 及義兵起，慶遠常居帷幄爲謀主。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, Qingyuan constantly remained within the command tent as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, Qingyuan constantly stayed in the command tent as chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 霸府建，以爲太尉從事中郎。

translations.literal: When the Pacification Office was established, he was made Aide of the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When the Pacification Office was established, he was made aide of the Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 高祖受禪，遷散騎常侍、右衛將軍，加征虜將軍，封重安侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication, Qingyuan was transferred to Regular Attendant and Right Guard General, with the additional title General Who Subdues Captives, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Chong'an with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Qingyuan was made Regular Attendant and Right Guard General, additionally General Who Subdues Captives, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Chong'an with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，以本官起之，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: He left office on his mother's mourning, was recalled to his former post, and firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his mother's mourning, was recalled to his former post, and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，遷中領軍，改封雲杜侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he was transferred to Commander of the Army and his enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Yundu.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianjian year 2 he was made Commander of the Army and re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Yundu.

sentences.zh: 四年，出爲使持節、都督雍梁南北秦四州諸軍事、征虜將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out as Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Yong, Liang, and the northern and southern Qin provinces, General Who Subdues Captives, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he went out as Bearer of the Staff, commander-in-chief of Yong, Liang, and northern and southern Qin, General Who Subdues Captives, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖餞於新亭，謂曰：「卿衣錦還鄉，朕無西顧之憂矣。」

translations.literal: Gaozu saw him off at Xinting and said: "You return home in brocade; I have no more worry for the west."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu saw him off at Xinting and said, "You return home in brocade; I need no longer look west with worry."

sentences.zh: 七年，徵爲護軍將軍，領太子庶子。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was summoned to be Protector of the Army and Concurrent Steward of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was summoned to be Protector of the Army and concurrent steward of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 未赴職，仍遷通直散騎常侍、右衛將軍，領右驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was transferred to Unhampered Regular Attendant, Right Guard General, and Concurrent General of the Right Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Before taking up the post he was transferred to Unhampered Regular Attendant, Right Guard General, and concurrent General of the Right Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 至京都，值魏宿預城請降，受詔爲援，於是假節守淮陰。

translations.literal: When he reached the capital, it happened that Wei's Suyu city asked to surrender; he received orders to go to its relief, and was given the staff pro tem to hold Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital, Wei's Suyu city asked to surrender; ordered to relieve it, he was given the staff pro tem to hold Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 魏軍退。

translations.literal: The Wei army withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八年，還京師，遷散騎常侍、太子詹事、雍州大中正。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he returned to the capital and was transferred to Regular Attendant, Steward of the Crown Prince, and Chief Rectifier of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he returned to the capital and was made Regular Attendant, steward of the crown prince, and chief rectifier of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷侍中、領軍將軍，給扶，幷鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Palace Attendant and Commander of the Army, with a cane and one set of martial pipes and drums.
translations.idiomatic: In year 10 he was made Palace Attendant and Commander of the Army, with a cane and one set of martial pipes and drums.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷安北將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and Inspector of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was made General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, and inspector of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 慶遠重爲本州，頗厲清節，士庶懷之。

translations.literal: Qingyuan again held his native province and was quite strict in integrity; scholars and commoners cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan again held his home province and was strict in integrity; officials and commoners cherished him.

sentences.zh: 明年春，卒，時年五十七。

translations.literal: The next spring he died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he died, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「念往篤終，前王令則；

translations.literal: Edict: "To recall the past and show depth at life's end is the former kings' settled norm;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "To honor the past and cherish the dead is the ancient kings' enduring rule;

sentences.zh: 式隆寵數，列代恒規。

translations.literal: to heighten favor and ranks is the constant practice of successive ages.
translations.idiomatic: to heighten favor and rank is the constant practice of every age.

sentences.zh: 使持節、都督雍梁南北秦四州郢州之竟陵司州之隨郡諸軍事、安北將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史、雲杜縣開國侯柳慶遠，器識淹曠，思懷通雅。

translations.literal: Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the military affairs of Yong, Liang, northern and southern Qin, Jingling in Yingzhou, and Suixiang in Sizhou, General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, Inspector of Yongzhou, and Marquis Who Founded the State of Yundu, Liu Qingyuan—his capacity and insight are broad and far-reaching, his thought humane and refined.
translations.idiomatic: Bearer of the Staff, commander-in-chief of Yong, Liang, northern and southern Qin, Jingling in Yingzhou, and Suixiang in Sizhou, General Who Pacifies the North, Pacify Barbarians Commandant, inspector of Yongzhou, and founding marquis of Yundu, Liu Qingyuan—his talent and insight are broad, his mind humane and refined.

sentences.zh: 爰初草昧，預屬經綸；

translations.literal: From the first in the founding struggle he shared in planning the enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: From the first days of the founding struggle he shared in planning the enterprise;

sentences.zh: 遠自升平，契闊禁旅。

translations.literal: from distant days in the age of peace he was bound to service in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: from long service in peaceful times he was bound to the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 重牧西籓，方弘治道，奄至殞喪，傷慟于懷。

translations.literal: Again he governed the western marches and was about to spread good rule, when suddenly death came—grief wounds my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Again he governed the western marches and was about to spread good rule, when death came suddenly—grief wounds my breast.

sentences.zh: 宜追榮命，以彰茂勳。

translations.literal: He should receive posthumous honors to display his abundant merit.
translations.idiomatic: Let posthumous honors be granted to display his abundant merit.

sentences.zh: 可贈侍中、中軍將軍、開府儀同三司，鼓吹、侯如故。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously made Palace Attendant, Central Army General, and Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes; martial pipes and drums and his marquisate are to remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made Palace Attendant, Central Army General, and Opener of the Mansion Equal to the Three Dukes; martial pipes and drums and his marquisate remain as before.

sentences.zh: 諡曰忠惠。

translations.literal: Posthumous name Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous name Zhonghui, "Loyal and Kind."

sentences.zh: 賻錢二十萬，布二百匹。

translations.literal: Funerary gift: two hundred thousand in cash and two hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Funerary gift: two hundred thousand cash and two hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 」及喪還京師，高祖出臨哭。

translations.literal: 」 When the coffin returned to the capital, Gaozu went out in person to mourn.
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin returned to the capital, Gaozu went out in person to mourn.

sentences.zh: 子津嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jin succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin succeeded.

sentences.zh: 初，慶遠從父兄衛將軍世隆嘗謂慶遠曰：「吾昔夢太尉以褥席見賜，吾遂亞台司，適又夢以吾褥席與汝，汝必光我公族。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qingyuan's paternal cousin, the General of the Guard Shilong, had once told Qingyuan: "I once dreamed the Grand Marshal gave me bedding; I then stood second to the Three Excellencies. Now I dream again that I gave you my bedding—you will surely bring glory to our clan."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qingyuan's paternal cousin, General of the Guard Shilong, had told him: "I once dreamed the Grand Marshal gave me bedding and I rose next to the Three Excellencies. Now I dream I gave you my bedding—you will surely honor our house."

sentences.zh: 」至是，慶遠亦繼世隆焉。

translations.literal: By then Qingyuan had indeed followed in Shilong's footsteps.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qingyuan had indeed followed in Shilong's footsteps.

sentences.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：王茂、曹景宗、柳慶遠雖世爲將家，然未顯奇節。

translations.literal: Chen Minister of the Secretariat Yao Cha said: Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, and Liu Qingyuan, though from military families for generations, had not yet shown extraordinary deeds.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen Minister of the Secretariat Yao Cha said: Wang Mao, Cao Jingzong, and Liu Qingyuan came from generations of generals yet had not yet shown extraordinary deeds.

sentences.zh: 梁興，因日月末光，以成所志，配迹方、邵，勒勳鐘鼎，偉哉！

translations.literal: When Liang arose, they rode the last light of the age to fulfill their ambitions—rivaling Fang and Shao, their merit engraved on bells and cauldrons. How grand!
translations.idiomatic: When Liang arose they caught the day's last light and achieved their aims—rivaling Fang Hu and Shao Yi, their deeds cut into bell and tripod. Magnificent!

sentences.zh: 昔漢光武全愛功臣，不過朝請、特進，寇、鄧、耿、賈咸不盡其器力。

translations.literal: In Han, Guangwu treated his meritorious ministers with full favor, yet granted them no more than Palace Attendant or Special Advance; Kou, Deng, Geng, and Jia never used their full capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Han's Guangwu cherished his merit-holders yet gave them only Palace Attendant or Special Advance; Kou, Deng, Geng, and Jia never exhausted their talents.

sentences.zh: 茂等迭據方岳，位終上將，君臣之際，邁於前代矣。

translations.literal: Mao and the others in turn held command of provinces, ending as supreme generals—the bond between ruler and minister surpassed the former age.
translations.idiomatic: Mao and the others in turn held provincial commands and died as supreme generals; the bond between throne and minister outdid earlier times.
